doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Relationships and a musician's life
summary: Hard to sustain relationships while traveling; she mentions Bucky and Ruth Pizzarelli, being single now, and hoping to remarry.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Is it hard with all the traveling and so forth and the way your life is, is it hard to have a established relationships?

Yes. I think every musician is going to say yes to this. If they so no, not really, then they’ve just got really lucky. I mean really. Because you see the wonderful relationships. You and I were at a dinner table with Bucky and Ruth. And it’s like you just take after them, hanging out together, having a good time together. It’s wonderful. It’s so wonderful to see but it’s also so rare. So yes, right now I’m single. I was married. But I have a wonderful guy in my life so I would definitely tie the knot again. It’s very hard. It’s been very hard for the last few years, just my whole life actually, just to understand that I’m a musician and I travel and I’m a little ambitious, and really this is my life. And I mean I have had boyfriends who say you can’t go away this much and well another reason is economic too, I’ve got to — living in New York ain’t cheap living by yourself.
You have to go where the work is.

You have to go where the work is, and often I’m going out of town to play with some people I really like playing with, I’m going to have fun, I’m not staying in town waiting for the phone call for the local gigs. I might not be doing something as great you know what I mean? No anyway, so it is hard. And now I’m in a relationship that I really want to — interview me in ten years. No but that I really want to see into marriage. I really want all that. It’s just really hard to have as a musician.
